raw_tool_response: User responded: model_context=For the first release, model context must remain strictly synthetic and local-only.  1. Synthetic questions and current conversation turns may be used transiently for the active interaction. 2. Only approved, valid, current and retrieval-eligible synthetic knowledge passages may be included for answer generation. 3. Synthetic ticket/customer fields may be used only when required for the specific classification, analysis or reporting purpose. 4. Internal notes may be included only when synthetic, explicitly authorized and necessary for the intended purpose. 5. Real customer data, personal information, confidential business data, credentials, secrets and unauthorized content must be excluded. 6. Draft/pending document classification under Q6 is limited to authorized ingestion and classification. It does not permit answer retrieval, knowledge citations or authoritative responses. 7. Persistent content-bearing conversation history, model memory and cross-session context storage are prohibited in the first release until a separate policy is explicitly approved. 8. Apply tenant authorization, lifecycle eligibility, data minimization and redaction before constructing model context. 9. Upon access revocation or deletion approval, immediately stop further retrieval and invalidate affected active context, caches and derived data. No deleted or unauthorized content may be reintroduced. 10. No external-provider transmission is permitted without separately approved PB-02 permissions.  These restrictions are mandatory and cannot be bypassed by model configuration or administrative privileges., history_persistence=For the first release, conversation, prompt and response persistence is prohibited. Adopt a transient-only model for the current authorized session.  1. User prompts, conversation turns, retrieved excerpts and AI-generated responses may exist only temporarily in memory for the active authorized interaction. 2. Do not persist conversation transcripts, prompts, responses, retrieved content or content-bearing interaction history in databases, files, caches or other persistent storage. 3. Temporary processing data must be discarded when the interaction/session ends or authorization is revoked, whichever occurs first. 4. Do not create persistent derived copies, embeddings or backups of conversation content. 5. Retain only content-free audit metadata under the separately approved 365-day audit retention policy. Permitted metadata may include tenant identifier, user identifier, event type, timestamp, action status and correlation identifier. 6. Audit records must never contain prompts, responses, document excerpts, personal information, credentials or other content-bearing data. 7. Any future persistent conversation-history capability requires a separate documented policy covering permitted fields, purpose, retention duration, deletion triggers, backup handling and tenant-scoped access controls, followed by independent approval.  No persistent conversation history or model memory is authorized in the first release. This decision does not modify the existing deletion, tenant isolation, authorization or external-provider restrictions., ownership_visibility=For the first release, persistent conversation history is prohibited. Therefore, no persistent conversation ownership, sharing, export or history-management capability is authorized.  1. The authenticated user who initiates an interaction may view and continue only their own active authorized session. 2. No other user may access or continue that session. 3. Support Agents and Support Managers have no general or manager-level conversation visibility. 4. Tenant Admin permissions are limited to account, tenant and role administration. Administrative status does not grant conversation-content access. 5. Knowledge Reviewers have no conversation-history access. 6. Platform Admin access to tenant conversation content is strictly prohibited. 7. Conversation sharing and export are not supported in the first release. 8. Active session content must be discarded when the session ends or authorization is revoked, whichever occurs first. 9. No persistent conversation recovery or restoration is permitted. 10. Only approved content-free audit metadata may be retained under the existing 365-day audit policy. 11. All access must enforce tenant isolation, user authentication and explicit authorization. No role-based privilege may bypass these restrictions.  Any future persistent history, manager visibility, sharing or export capability requires a separate documented policy, explicit permission definitions and independent approval., feedback_notes=For the first release, feedback is limited to non-persistent, structured feedback mechanisms.  1. Users may provide simple ratings such as Thumbs Up/Down and predefined feedback categories for the current interaction. 2. Free-text feedback and persistent content-bearing feedback storage are deferred until a separate policy is approved. 3. Feedback may be processed transiently for the purpose of evaluating the current interaction, but must not be used for automatic model training, fine-tuning or model improvement. 4. Synthetic ticket/customer context may be included in model context only when explicitly required for an authorized classification, analysis or response-generation purpose. Processing must remain synthetic, local-only and transient. 5. Internal notes must not be persistently stored or transmitted to the model in the first release. Any future use requires explicit authorization, defined purpose, tenant-scoped access and retention controls. 6. Feedback must not automatically approve knowledge, change document lifecycle status, modify ticket classifications or reinstate excluded sources. 7. Feedback authorship and visibility must remain restricted to the authenticated user and their authorized active session. 8. Do not store prompts, responses, feedback text or content-bearing notes in audit records. Only permitted content-free audit metadata may be retained under the existing 365-day audit policy. 9. Any future free-text feedback, internal-note persistence, analytics storage or model-training capability requires a separately documented policy and independent approval.  All existing synthetic/local-only, tenant-isolation, authorization, deletion and no-external-provider-transmission restrictions remain unchanged., sensitive_data_logs=For the first release, implement strict sensitive-content detection, minimization and rejection controls.  1. Real personal data, customer information, credentials, passwords, API keys, access tokens, secrets and confidential business information are prohibited in model context. 2. Apply input validation and sensitive-content detection before any content is processed by the AI model. 3. Where sensitive information is detected, reject the affected input or safely redact the sensitive fields before processing. If safe redaction cannot be reliably established, reject the input entirely. 4. Do not expose rejected sensitive content in error messages, diagnostic output, telemetry or user notifications. Provide a generic notification explaining that the input contains prohibited sensitive information. 5. Do not persist rejected input or create diagnostic copies containing sensitive content. 6. Application logs, telemetry, traces and error records must not contain prompts, responses, source excerpts, personal information, credentials, secrets or internal notes. 7. Permitted operational and audit fields are limited to content-free metadata such as tenant identifier, user identifier, event type, timestamp, validation outcome, error category and correlation identifier. 8. Sensitive-content incidents must generate a content-free security event for authorized operational review. Any incident investigation must follow separately approved access and evidence-handling procedures. 9. Do not retain sensitive content by default for debugging, analytics, troubleshooting or model improvement. 10. All controls must apply consistently across application services, model context construction, temporary storage, caches, telemetry and exports. 11. No external-provider transmission is permitted. Any future exception requires separate PB-02 approval and documented security/privacy controls.  Existing synthetic/local-only processing, tenant isolation, deletion requirements and content-free audit retention restrictions remain unchanged., retention_authority=For the first release, privacy, conversation-history access and retention policies must follow independent approval and separation-of-duties principles.  1. A designated Privacy/Security Owner may propose privacy, retention, history-access and exception policies. 2. A separately designated authorized Privacy/Security Approver must independently review and approve these policies. The proposer must not approve their own proposal. 3. Authorized Development and Operations teams may implement only explicitly approved policies. Implementation does not confer policy-approval authority. 4. Q5 deletion requirements remain mandatory, including immediate retrieval exclusion and the applicable 24-hour physical-purge obligation following the defined authorized deletion trigger. 5. Encrypted backup age-out remains 30 days, subject to the approved backup lifecycle policy. Any restoration must reapply deletion and access restrictions before restored data becomes accessible. 6. Content-free audit metadata may be retained for 365 days. This does not authorize retention of prompts, responses, conversation transcripts, source excerpts or other content-bearing records. 7. Legal holds require documented authorization by an appropriately designated legal authority. A legal hold does not automatically grant retrieval, processing or user-access permission. 8. Release of a legal hold must trigger the applicable deletion obligations without silently resetting or waiving the original deletion deadline. 9. Persistent conversation history, content-bearing interaction storage and retention exceptions remain prohibited in the first release. 10. Any future privacy, history-access, retention or legal-hold exception requires documented purpose, exact data scope, authorized owner, independent approval, duration, deletion conditions and audit evidence. 11. No Platform Admin role may access tenant content or override tenant isolation, deletion or privacy restrictions.  Any unresolved retention schedule, exception mechanism or additional content-bearing storage capability remains explicitly deferred and must not proceed until its policy is independently approved. Existing synthetic/local-only and PB-02 restrictions remain unchanged., rationale_deferrals=The first-release privacy policy follows a strict data-minimization, transient-processing and least-privilege approach.  The primary objective is to demonstrate the AI-assisted functionality without introducing unnecessary privacy, data-retention, compliance or external-provider risks.  Confirmed first-release decisions:  1. Model context is restricted to authorized synthetic/local-only data. 2. Conversation prompts, responses, retrieved excerpts and interaction history are transient only. Persistent content-bearing conversation storage is prohibited. 3. Conversation sharing, export, cross-session history and persistent model memory are not supported. 4. Only structured, non-persistent feedback is permitted. Free-text feedback and feedback-based model training are prohibited. 5. Real customer data, personal information, credentials, secrets and confidential business information are prohibited. 6. Sensitive-content detection, rejection/redaction and content-free security logging are mandatory. 7. Only approved content-free audit metadata may be retained under the existing 365-day audit policy. 8. Existing deletion, encrypted-backup age-out, legal-hold, tenant-isolation and authorization requirements remain unchanged. 9. External-provider transmission and Platform Admin tenant-content access remain prohibited.  Explicitly deferred decisions:  - Persistent conversation history and user-level model memory. - Conversation sharing, export and manager visibility. - Free-text feedback and internal-note persistence. - External AI provider data processing, contractual safeguards and provider retention. - Data residency, cross-border processing and jurisdiction-specific compliance requirements. - Any persistent analytics containing interaction or customer content. - Future model-training or fine-tuning permissions. - Additional retention schedules, legal-hold exceptions and content-bearing audit requirements.  Each deferred capability requires a separate documented policy, defined data scope, privacy/security assessment, appropriate authority, independent approval and applicable technical controls before it can proceed.  Deferral does not create implied permission, default approval or an exception to existing restrictions.  These decisions clarify first-release requirements only. They do not approve the PRD, authorize implementation, testing, deployment, runtime access or initiation of another process.

material_confirmation.rationale_context: rationale_deferrals lists free-text feedback and internal-note persistence as deferred, but does not resolve model transmission.
material_confirmation.materiality: One field conditionally permits synthetic internal notes in model context, another prohibits first-release transmission. Selecting either silently changes actual policy/permission.
